articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Fall Cleanup Across Kettle Hill
articles.deck: Residents of Kettle Hill filled the hall on Thursday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Mildred Dunmore, who has lived in Kettle Hill for 8 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The plan calls for stormwater drain repair along Elm Drive, with work expected to start in February.
Public works estimates the work will take about 8 weeks once it begins. Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Thursday mornings.

articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Summer Cleanup Across Mill Hill
articles.deck: Residents of Mill Hill filled the hall on Monday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The Mill Hill Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
The group has raised $12,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. Public works estimates the work will take about 31 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Agnes Cifuentes, 80, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Agnes Cifuentes for the many years of service to Foxglove Heights.
body: Agnes Cifuentes died in September at home on Pine Avenue, at the age of 80. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Upper Commons Historical Society in his or her name.

Born in Foxglove Heights in the years after the war, Agnes Cifuentes spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Foxglove Heights.

articles.title: Roman Nowicki Retires After 7 Years at the Mill Hill Lions Club
articles.deck: Organizers expect about 7 people and say community garden is the main draw.
body: Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Tuesday mornings. Several residents on Salem Street said they had been waiting since 1991 for something like this.
Roman Nowicki, who has lived on Salem Street for 7 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
The effort began in August when a handful of neighbors met at the Foundry Row fire house to talk about community garden.

articles.title: Budget Hearing Draws 5 Residents
articles.deck: The vote came after 5 residents spoke at Tuesday’s session.
body: Residents of Kettle Hill said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Councilmember Lorraine Kaczmarek asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $18,500.

articles.title: Canal Park Residents Push for Tool Library
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 34 weeks and will be paid for with $48,000 raised locally.
body: Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Kettle Hill Park gate on Saturday at 7 p.m. Several residents on Keystone Drive said they had been waiting since 1987 for something like this.

The effort began in June when a handful of neighbors met at the Kettle Hill Park gate to talk about tool library. Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Saturday mornings.

The group has raised $48,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. Vincent Kaczmarek, who has lived on Keystone Drive for 34 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.title: Cedar Hollow Primary Adds Saturday Cleanup Day to Winter Schedule
articles.deck: The program begins in May and is open to all students in grade 7 and up.
body: Principal Simone Emerson said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers. Students will meet on Saturday afternoons in the Cedar Hollow Pavilion, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.
Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for May.

articles.deck: The work is expected to take 36 weeks and will be paid for with $3,400 raised locally.
body: Joseph McIver, who has lived on Vine Street for 36 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Millrace library on Friday at 7 p.m. Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Friday mornings.
